newsitem.title: UK: Minorco profits up despite price weakness.
newsitem.headline: Minorco profits up despite price weakness.

text.p: International mining-to-paper group Minorco SA on Wednesday reported a nine percent rise in 1996 underlying earnings as higher gold, copper and newsprint production offset the impact of weak commodities prices.

Minorco, controlled by South African giants De Beers and Anglo American, said 1996 net earnings rose to $396.4 million from $365.0 million the previous year. The 1996 figure excludes a $60.7 million charge, mainly stemming from two restructuring operations.
Minorco said sharply lower commodity prices depressed operating earnings by about $150 million.
But, Minorco said, acquisitions in its European industrial minerals division, principally Tilcon, contributed to the overall underlying earnings increase.
Operating profits rose in Minorco's base metal mining operations, in industrial minerals as well as paper and packaging, but fell in the agribusiness segment. They were basically flat in gold mining.

Chairman Julian Ogilvie Thompsom said Minorco would continue to focus on its mining operations for overall growth after recent efforts to boost the sector's competitiveness. ($ = 0.623 British Pounds)
